title: Dreams & Dream Interpretations (Part 1)
arabic:
أَلآ إِنَّ أَوْلِيَآءَ اللَّهِ لاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا وَكَانُوا يَتَّقُونَ لَهُمُ الْبُشْرَي فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَفِي الاَخِرَةِ لا تَبْدِيلَ لِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ

قال الرؤيا الصالحةُ يراها المسلم أو تُرَى له عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ الرُّؤْيَا الْحَسَنَةُ مِنَ الرَّجُلِ الصَّالِحِ جُزْءٌ مِنْ سِتَّةٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ جُزْءًا مِنَ النُّبُوَّةِ ‏"‏‏‏

قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ الرُّؤْيَا ثَلاَثٌ فَرُؤْيَا حَقٌّ وَرُؤْيَا يُحَدِّثُ بِهَا الرَّجُلُ نَفْسَهُ وَرُؤْيَا تَحْزِينٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ فَمَنْ رَأَى مَا يَكْرَهُ فَلْيَقُمْ فَلْيُصَلِّ

فَإِذَا رَأَى أَحَدُكُمُ الشَّىْءَ يَكْرَهُهُ فَلْيَنْفُثْ عَنْ يَسَارِهِ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ إِذَا اسْتَيْقَظَ وَلْيَتَعَوَّذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شَرِّهَا فَإِنَّهَا لَنْ تَضُرَّهُ

عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ الرُّؤْيَا مِنَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحُلْمُ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ ‏" إِنْ كُنْتُ لأَرَى الرُّؤْيَا أَثْقَلَ عَلَىَّ مِنْ جَبَلٍ

فَمَاهُوَ إِلاَّ أَنْ سَمِعْتُ بِهَذَا الْحَدِيثِ فَمَا أُبَالِيهَا عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ إِذَا رَأَى أَحَدُكُمْ رُؤْيَا يُحِبُّهَا فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ مِنَ اللَّهِ، فَلْيَحْمَدِ اللَّهَ عَلَيْهَا، وَلْيُحَدِّثْ بِهَا، وَإِذَا رَأَى غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا يَكْرَهُ، فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ، فَلْيَسْتَعِذْ مِنْ شَرِّهَا، وَلاَ يَذْكُرْهَا لأَحَدٍ، فَإِنَّهَا لاَ تَضُرُّهُ

لَا تَقْصُصْ رُءْيَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُوا۟ لَكَ كَيْدًا ۖ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنَ لِلْإِنسَـٰنِ عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ مَنْ رَآنِي فِي الْمَنَامِ فَقَدْ رَآنِي، فَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ لاَ يَتَخَيَّلُ بي

أَنَّ رِجَالاً، مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أُرُوا لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ فِي الْمَنَامِ فِي السَّبْعِ الأَوَاخِرِ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ أَرَى رُؤْيَاكُمْ قَدْ تَوَاطَأَتْ فِي السَّبْعِ الأَوَاخِرِ، فَمَنْ كَانَ مُتَحَرِّيَهَا فَلْيَتَحَرَّهَا فِي السَّبْعِ الأَوَاخِرِ ‏"‏‏

رؤي اليل مثل رؤي النهار قال‏:‏ ‏"‏إذا اقترب الزمان لم تكد رؤيا المؤمن تكذب، ورؤيا المؤمن جزء من ستة وأربعين جزءاً من النبوة‏"‏ وَقَالَ لِلَّذِى ظَنَّ أَنَّهُۥ نَاجٍ مِّنْهُمَا

عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَال من تَحَلَّمَ بِحُلُمٍ لَمْ يَرَهُ، كُلِّفَ أَنْ يَعْقِدَ بَيْنَ شَعِيرَتَينِ يوم القيامة ثُمَّ أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ أَيَّتُهَا ٱلْعِيرُ إِنَّكُمْ لَسَـٰرِقُونَ
english:
Dreams and dream interpretations by Imām Anwar Awlaqi رحمه الله. This series of lectures covers the many different aspects from the world of the unseen, as one of the early scholars in Islām (اسلام), Ibn Qutaybah رحمه الله once said, there is nothing that people deal with from different sciences that is more obscure, delicate, Exalted, noble, difficult and problematic than dreams, because they are a type of Revelation and they are kind of Prophethood. We hope you enjoy this series of lectures.

Allāh ﷻ says, “Behold, verily on the Friends of Allāh ﷻ, the Awliyā (أولياء) of Allāh ﷻ, there's no fear, nor shall they grieve. Those who believe and constantly guard against evil, for them are glad tidings, in the life of the present and the hereafter, no change can there be in the words of Allāh ﷻ. This is indeed the supreme Felicity.”

So Allāh ﷻ in these āyāt, says that, His Awliyā (أؤلياء), the friends of Allāh ﷻ, there shall be no fear on them, or grief.

Glad Tidings in the Form of Good Dream: And then Allāh ﷻ says, lahum bushra fil hayāti duniyā wal ākhirah, (لَهُمُ الْبُشْرَي فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَفِي الاَخِرَةِ) for them are glad tidings in the life of the present and in the hereafter. So, what are the glad tidings, for the believers in this life? Imām Ahmad bin Hanbal رحمه الله in his Musnad, (مسند) narrates Hadīth by Abū Darda رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, that Rusūlullāh ﷺ said, in the Tafsīr of this āyah (آية), lahum bushra fil hayāti duniyā wal ākhirah,

In the explanation of this āyah (آية), that the glad tidings, that the believer receives in this life, is a good dream that he sees, or somebody sees for him. So, for example, if someone saw a dream for you, and its good news for you, this is a bushrā (بشرٰى), this is a glad tiding from Allāh ﷻ, or it could be a dream that you yourself see. So, we're going to talk about this interesting and amazing world of the unseen because it's part of ghayb (غيب), dreams are part of the unseen, metaphysical world, something that is beyond the material world. And it's a very interesting and intriguing world.

Two Extremes in the Issue of Dreams: Now, regarding the issue of dreams, there are two extremes: There is one extreme, where some deviants from this Ummah exaggerated in the issue of the importance of dreams and they made false claims based on false dreams. And we will talk about the issue of dreams and Sharīah (شريعة) that the dreams have nothing to do with Sharīah (شريعة). We cannot derive laws, for example, halāl (حلال) and harām (حرام) from dreams.

And then there's the other extreme, where they, some people view that this issue is totally nonsense. It doesn't mean anything. But there's a middle ground. And we'll talk about In Shā Allāh (ان شآء الله) in these lectures, some rules and regulations and notes regarding the topic of dreams in Islām (اسلام), and we'll talk a little bit about the issue of dream interpretation too, towards the end.

Good Dream, a Part of Prophethood: Anas Ibn Mālik رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه says, that Rusulullāh ﷺ said, that the good dream, seen by a righteous man is one part of 46 parts of Prophethood.

So, the issue carries some importance in Islām (اسلام) and we'll see that Allāh ﷻ talks about dreams and Qur’ān (قرآن). For example, in Sūrah Yūsuf, you have the dream of Sayyīdanā Yūsuf عليه السلام, when he was young and then you have the dream of the two prisoners who were with Sayyīdanā Yūsuf عليه السلام, in jail, and then you have the dream of the king. There's also a dream mentioned, that Rusulullāh ﷺ saw, and then we'll also talk about dreams that were mentioned in Hadīth (حديث) dreams that were seen by Rusulullāh ﷺ, dreams that were seen by the Sahābah (صحابة) and some dreams that were seen by As Sālihīn (الصالحين), in this Hadīth (حديث), Rusulullāh ﷺ says, that it's part of 46 parts of Prophethood.

There are some scholars who tried to give an explanation to this particular ratio, why is it one part of 46? this is an explanation that they gave, we have no way of discerning, whether it is right or not, because there there's no evidence from Hadīth (حديث) to state that this is the fact for sure, but I will mention it as an explanation that was given by some scholars obviously, the issue is disputed, some scholars don't agree with it. But they said that the prophethood of Rusulullāh ﷺ, the period in which he was given the Nubuwwah (نبؤة), extends from the age of 40 to the age of 63. So, it's 23 years. Because we know that Rusulullāh ﷺ received Nubuwwah (نبؤة), Prophethood when he was 40 years old and he passed away when he was 63, So the period is 23 years.

And we also know from Sīrah (سيرة) that Rusulullāh ﷺ for six months before becoming a prophet, for six months, he ﷺ was seeing dreams on a very frequent basis and the dreams were direct and they would occur exactly as he would see them, ((كفلق الصبح and as was mentioned in the Hadīth (حديث), so the dreams were very frequent and very direct. So, what's the ratio of six months to 23? The ratio is one to 46. Anyway, this is the part of Nubuwwah (نبؤة), that remains until the end of time, dreams that the believers see. So, we'll talk about some rules and notes regarding dreams and dream interpretation. 0

Books of Scholars on Dream Interpretations: First, I'll quote to you a saying, by one of the earliest scholars of As Salaf(السلف), his name is Ibn Qutaybah al Dīnawarī رحمه الله. Ibn Qutaybah al Dīnawarī رحمه الله is one of the Scholars of Ahlus Sunnah (اهل السنة), very early scholar and he has a book on dream interpretation and it's one of the earliest books written on the subject. By the way, there’s a book that is attributed to Ibn Sīrīn, is called dream interpretation by Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله. That book is not actually written by Ibn Sīrīn, himself. The book contains a lot of narrations to Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله, but it wasn't authored and penned by Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله, himself. In fact, it was written centuries after Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله, passed away and it was written by a Shāfī’ scholar, he was called Al Wā’f.

So, Ibn Qutaybah رحمه الله has a book on dream interpretation. He says in this book, arabic and he says there's nothing that people deal with, from the different sciences, (he means the sciences of Sharīah(شريعة), he says, there's nothing that people deal with, from the different sciences that is more obscure, and delicate, and exalted and noble and difficult and problematic than dreams, because it is a type of Revelation and a kind of Prophethood. So, it's really not the light issue. And it's not a very simple one either. He doesn't see that there's anything that is more obscure and delicate and exalted and noble in the same time, and difficult and problematic. Why? He says because it is part of Prophethood. So therefore, dream interpretation is not an easy thing at all.

Types of Dreams: There are three types of dreams.

At Tirmidhi(الترمزي) narrates, and Muhammad ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله, he narrates from Abū hurayrah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, Ibn Sīrīn is a Tabī’(تابعي) he's one of the Tab’īn(تابعين), he studied under the Sahābah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنهم,

Rusulullāh ﷺ says, that there are three types of dreams: The first is a true dream (ru’yā haq).

The second رُؤْيَا يُحَدِّثُ بِهَا الرَّجُلُ نَفْسَهُ, a dream in which a person is speaking to himself. What does this mean? He might be obsessed with something, or you might have thought about something for a long time during the daytime, you end up dreaming about it at night. This really doesn't mean anything. It is repetition of your thoughts during daytime.

The third type is, رُؤْيَا تَحْزِينٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ and the third type is a dream from shaytan. That is the Tahzīn(تحزين). He wants to make you sad. He inspires to you a dream that would make you feel bad that would make you sad. Why would shaytān do this? because he hates the believer. That's why we have in the Hadīth (حديث) in Sahīh Muslim (صحيح مسلم) that whenever a child is born shaytān stabs the child and that's why the child comes out to this world crying. It's because of that stab of shaytān, I mean look at how envious this being is, I mean he wouldn't even leave the newborn child alone. That's how bad he really hates the son of Ādam عليه السلام. So, these are the three types of dreams.

What should You Do if You See a Bad Dream?

And also, Rusulullāh ﷺ says, when you see a dream from shaytān (شيطان), what should you do? Stand up and pray وَلْيَقُمْ فَلْيُصَلِّ And in another Hadīth (حديث), Rusulullāh ﷺ said, you turn towards the left side and you blow three times and you seek refuge in Allāh ﷻ from the evil of such a dream and it will not harm you. Rusulullāh ﷺ says,

that you blow towards the left and you say, أَعُوْذُ بِاللّٰهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطٰانِ الرَّجِيْم, you seek refuge in Allāh ﷻ from this dream, it won't harm you then it won't harm you.

“The good dream is from Allāh ﷻ and the hulm ((حلم is from shaytān (شيطان).” In the Arabic language there is a differentiation between the good dream and the dream that is from shaytān (شيطان). So, the ru’yā(رؤيا), when the word Ru’yā(رؤيا), is used usually means a good dream. And when the word Hulm(حلم) is used, it usually means something that doesn't have the meaning or it is from shaytān(شيطان) .

Abu Salamah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, one of the Sahābah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنهم and his statement will show you that how does Sahābah(صحابة) would be concerned when they see a dream, Abū Salamah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه said,

He said sometimes I would see a dream that would be heavier on my shoulder than carrying a mountain. Meaning he would be so concerned with it. He said when he heard this Hadīth(حديث),

But since I heard this Hadīth(حديث), I wouldn't care about a bad dream that I would see is referring to this Hadīth (حديث) that I just mentioned where Rusulullāh ﷺ says that a good dream is from Allāh ﷻ and a bad dream is from shaytān (شيطان).

How to Deal with Dreams: There's another advice that also Rusulullāh ﷺ gives us on how to deal with dreams: Rusulullāh ﷺ says, “when one of you sees a dream that he likes, it is from Allāh ﷻ and he should thank Allāh ﷻ for it, and he should speak about it. And if he sees otherwise, meaning, if you see something that you don't like, it is from shaytān (شيطان), seek refuge in Allāh ﷻ from its harm and don't mention it to anybody, and it won't harm you.”

So, when you see a good dream, you can talk about it. And we will talk about who you can mention the dream to, you don't talk about it with everyone. And if it's not a good dream, then forget about it and don't mention it to anyone. This is an important advice to note here. Don't tell anybody about it. Don't give shaytān (شيطان) a laugh. Make him see that you're concerned and you're sad and you're sorry and you're complaining about this dream to this person and that person. completely forget about it and don't talk about it to anyone seek refuge in Allāh ﷻ from Shaytān (شيطان) and from the harm of that dream. And don't mention it to anyone. So again, to recap on what we just mentioned, when you see a good dream, you thank Allāh ﷻ for it and you can talk about it and when you see something that is not good from shaytān (شيطان), then Rusulullāh ﷺ says in one hadith, you stand up and pray, and another Hadīth (حديث), he ﷺ says that you blow towards left side, three times and you seek refuge in Allāh ﷻ and in the other Hadīth (حديث), Rusulullāh ﷺ says, don’t mention it to anyone.

Is every Dream that a Believer sees, Is it Good?

A question here, is every dream that a believer sees, Is it good? Al Muhallab رحمه الله says and this is from Ibn Hajar رحمه الله in his commentary on Sahīh al Bukhāri, He says araby ***

see because we mentioned in the Hadīth (حديث), that there are three types of dreams, one of them is the good dream that is seen by the believer. So, this exact means that every dream that the believer sees has a meaning that we mentioned that some of them would just be a reflection of the thoughts that you're thinking about or something that concerns you or something that the person might be obsessed with, he would dream about that frequently. So, Al Muhallab رحمه الله says, araby** He says, most of the dreams of the righteous people are good dreams. Because sometimes a righteous person could see a dream that is meaningless but that is not very frequent. Why? because he said that Shaytān’s control on them, is weak. Araby**. And the opposite is true with other people, because Shaytān (شيطان) has a stronger grasp on them.

Categories of People: Araby** He says, people are three categories araby** The Prophets: He said, the Ambiyā (أنبياء), the Prophets, all of their dreams are true dreams. But sometimes they need interpretation because we'll talk about here.

Two Categories of Good Dream: The good dream divides into two categories: One is a directory, meaning you would see something and the exact scene which you saw in your dream would repeat itself during the daytime, when you're awake. So, this dream is a direct dream, and it doesn't need any interpretation.

But then there is a good dream that comes in symbols and it needs to be interpreted.

Righteous People: And then he says, araby** And then you have the righteous people. And most of the time, their dreams are righteous dreams, araby** And sometimes their dreams are direct. So, the Ambiyā (أنبياء) all of their dreams are true. And most of them are direct with the righteous, most of their dreams are true and most of them need to be interpreted.

Rest of the People: Araby** And the rest of people, most of their dreams are not true. But some of them could be true. Because for example, in Sūrah Yūsuf, the king saw a dream, and he wasn't a Muslim, and those prisoners saw true dreams, and they weren't Muslim. So, a fāsiq (فاسق) Muslim who was not practicing, or a disbeliever could see a dream and it would be a true dream. So true, dreams are not exclusive to the believers. It's just that it's more frequent for them. So that's the first point.

Do not Mention the Dream for Interpretation except to a Scholar or a person who would Advise you Sincerely: Do not mention the dream for interpretation except to a scholar or a person who would advise you sincerely. So, you don't narrate your dream for the purpose of interpretation except to a person who has some expertise in the field, a scholar in this particular field because not every scholar has the ability to interpret dreams. Subhān Allāh(سبحان الله)! this is a gift from Allāh ﷻ, obviously part of it is knowledge. There’re parts of it that could be studied from books. But then there's another part of it that is a gift from Allāh ﷻ and there are some people in our Ummah that were famous with their ability to interpret dreams. And then you have some other great Scholars, it wasn't known that they had disability. So, for example, Abū Bakr رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه was famous for his ability to interpret dreams, ‘Umar Bin Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه and Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله was also famous for his ability to interpret dreams.

Rusulullāh ﷺ says that you should not mention your dream to an envious person. And there's evidence for this in Qur’ān, when Yūsuf عليه السلام saw his dream, and he was young at the time, and he mentioned to his father, his father told him,

His father, Ya’qūb عليه السلام told him, do not mention your dream to your brothers, why? فَيَكِيدُوا۟ لَكَ كَيْدًا they would plot against you out of envy.

So, we should not mention our dreams towards an envious person you should mention the dream towards the person whom you love, Rusulullāh ﷺ said, من تحب, if you love someone, then you can tell them your good dreams. And you mentioned the dream to a Nāsih (ناصح) a person who would give you sincere advice and to Ālim, to a scholar who would interpret it for you.

Seeing Rusulullāh ﷺ: Anas Ibn Mālik رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه says and this Hadīth (حديث) in Sahīh Al Bukhāri, Rusulullāh ﷺ says, “whoever sees me in his dream has seen me because Shaytān does not come in my form.”

What if the Description of Person is Different than Description of Rusulullāh ﷺ?

There's an issue here. What if a person sees Rusulullāh ﷺ in his dream, so he sees a person and his feeling in his dream tell him that this is Rusulullāh ﷺ but the description of this person is different than the description we have of Rusulullāh ﷺ. So, for example, you see somebody who has a grey beard. We know from the description of Rusulullāh ﷺ, that most of the beard of Rusulullāh ﷺ was black, except some of it grew grey. Is that Rusulullāh ﷺ? you see a person who is thin in your dream, and you think that’s Rusulullāh ﷺ? We know from the description of Rusulullāh ﷺ in the books that he was medium built. So, is that person in your dream Rusulullāh ﷺ?

Az Zuhri رحمه الله says, that Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله said, araby** If you see Rusulullāh ﷺ according to his description. So according to the view of Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله, you have only seen Rusulullāh ﷺ, if you see him according to the description of Rusulullāh ﷺ that we have in books. And know however, has a contrary view as long as you felt in your dream that the person you saw was Rusulullāh ﷺ then it's Rusulullāh ﷺ if he comes in a different form. So, there's a difference of opinion here. According to a Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله and also Ibn Taymiyyah رحمه الله, you must see him according to his known descriptions.

But according to An Nawawi رحمه الله and some other scholars as long as you see him and your feeling is that this is also Rusulullāh ﷺ then it is Rusulullāh ﷺ. So, as you see, there is a difference of opinion on this point. By the way with the issue of seeing Rusulullāh ﷺ, not every believer will see Rusulullāh ﷺ. It's not a requirement and condition of being a Mu’min (مؤمن) that you see Rusulullāh ﷺ. It's Nai’mah(blessing) from Allāh ﷻ that some people see Rusulullāh ﷺ, and there are many believers who don't in fact, the majority don't. So, it should not be taken as proof of a person’s Īmān (أيمان), to see Rusulullāh ﷺ, or doesn't see him ﷺ and it's not something that is given to every person. Some people see Rusulullāh ﷺ very frequently, for example, Anas Ibn Mālik رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, it is mentioned that he used to see Rusulullāh ﷺ on a nightly basis, while some never see him ﷺ in their lifetime.

Repetition of Dream is a Sign of Truth: A repetition of a dream is a sign of its truth, whether the same person frequently sees that dream or more than one person, have the same dream. Ibn ‘Umar رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه said,

Abdullāh Ibn ‘Umar رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه says that more than one companion came to Rusulullāh ﷺ and narrated to him that they have dreamed that the night of Qadar(قدر) is in the last seven nights of Ramadān. So Rusulullāh ﷺ said, I see that your dreams Tawātāt (تواطات) meaning have strengthened each other that the night of Qadar(قدر) is towards the last seven nights of Ramadān(رمضان), so whoever is searching for it should search for it, in those seven nights. So, Rusulullāh ﷺ took it as an indication of the truth of the dream that more than one person sought.

And also, in the dream about Adhān (أذان). It is mentioned that ‘Umar Al Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه saw the dream and another companion from Al Ansār also saw that dream, so Rusulullāh ﷺ said, it is from Allāh ﷻ. So that's number four.

When is the most Expected Time to See a Righteous Dream: When is the most expected time to see a righteous dream? Is it at night? Or is it during daytime? And if you see a dream at night, are all the times equal? Whether you saw it towards the beginning of the night or towards the latter part of it? What if you see a dream after Fajr(فجر)? What if you see a dream at noontime? What is it with dreams during the daytime? Do they have any meaning at all? Well, Ibn Sīrīn says,

And this is in  Sahīh Bukhārī (صحيح بخاري) that Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله says that the dreams of daytime are equal to the dreams of night. Because some people say that you must see the dream at night if you see it during the daytime, it's meaningless. No, that's not true. Any part of the day or night can be a time in which you see a true dream. However, some scholars stated that the best time during the night-time is before Fajr(فجر) and the best time in the daytime is at noon the time of قيلولة when you take a nap, a midday nap, that is the best time during the day.

Two Types of true Dreams: True dreams are two types direct dreams that do not need interpretation and dreams that are symbols that need to be interpreted. We talked about this before.

Ibn Battāl رحمه الله Categorization: I’ll mention it to you what Ibn Battāl رحمه الله said, one of our scholars, he said araby He says, “dreams are two types.”

He's talking about the true dream, a clear, evident dream, like somebody who would dream about himself, giving dates to someone. And during the daytime, he would give somebody dates. So, what he saw at night, repeated itself in the daytime. He said this type of dream doesn't need any interpretation because it just happens as you saw it.

And then he says there's another type of dream, Marmuzah (مرموزة) which comes in symbols. And this type, you would not understand its meaning unless you interpreted with this person who has knowledge and experience with dream interpretation. Because the symbols are very delicate and sometimes very sophisticated or complicated. So, this type of dream needs to be interpreted because it comes in symbols. For example, when Rusulullāh ﷺ saw that he was drinking milk, and then there was some milk that remained in the bottom of the vessel and then he gave that vessel to ‘Umar Al Khattāb رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه to drink and Rusulullāh ﷺ said, the interpretation of that dream is knowledge. So here milk symbolises knowledge. This is a dream that didn't happen as it was seen. The meaning of this dream is not that Rusulullāh ﷺ would physically actually drink that milk, but it means that he has absorbed knowledge. And Rusulullāh ﷺ said, in the dream that it was so much that milk started to flow from beneath his nails, his fingers. So, he had so much knowledge absorbed in him that it started flowing out of him. So, this is a symbol, milk, here's a symbol of knowledge.

Dreams can be about the Past, the Present or the Future: Dreams can be about the past, or the present, or the future. You could dream about something that happened in the past, or you could dream about something that is happening now. Or you could dream about something that is in the future.

True Dreams Increase towards the End of Time: True dreams increase Towards the end of time, Muhammad Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله said, that he heard that Abū Hurayrah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه says and this is in Sahīh Bukhāri (and Muslim)

Abū Hurayrah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه said that Rusulullāh ﷺ said, “when time approaches that is the literal translation of إقترب الزمان when time approaches, the dream of the believer rarely would lie.”

When Time Approaches… is Explained in Two Different Opinions: Meaning that the dream of the believer is true when time approaches. So, what does this statement mean? time approaches? there are two explanations given:

Araby Al Khattābi رحمه الله says that the meaning of   إقترب الزمان)) when time approaches, is the time of night and the time of day, when the time of night approaches the length of the time of daytime, that is when the dreams are true. And when does this happen in our area in our part of the world. This happens in spring and in fall, because in summer, the daytime is long. And in winter, the night-time is long. So daytime and night-time approach each other in terms of length during the springtime and during fall. And these are the two times when flowers open up and when fruits are ripe. And the scholars of dream interpretation actually state that these are the two times when the dreams are its most expected, most likely, that dreams would be true. So, this is one opinion.

The other opinion is towards the end of time.

And Al Qurtubi رحمه الله says araby what is meant by this Hadīth is the end of time and it's talking about the band of the believers that will be with the ‘Īsā Ibn Maryam عليه السلام after he kills Ad-Dajjāl(الدجال). So, this is a statement by Al Qurtubi رحمه الله.

And Ibn Abī Jamrah رحمه الله, this is a scholar from Al Andalus(الاندلسية). He says, araby He says the reason why the believer sees true dreams in that time is because the believer will be Gharīb (غريب), he will be alone, as was mentioned in the Hadīth (حديث), إِنَّ الإِسْلاَمَ بَدَأَ غَرِيبًا وَسَيَعُودُ غَرِيبًا

And then Ibn Hajar al-‘Asqalāniرحمه الله comes all of this and says, whenever the times are difficult for the believer, he will see dreams that are true more frequently because he needs help. When the believer is alone, when the times are difficult, when you don't find people support you on truth, on haqq (حق), that is when Allāh ﷻ will inspire you and give you glad tidings through true dreams that you would see and this is to give the believers in those difficult and testing times, it gives the believers strength. It gives them confidence; it gives them hope. So, they would see a lot of dreams that come true. And that is why we see that for example the Muslims who are being tested. For example, we see that the believers who are in jail, in prison they see a lot of dreams and also those who are fighting fī sabīlillāh (في سبيل الله) they see a lot of dreams why because they are being tested by Allāh ﷻ so Allāh ﷻ assist them. Allāh ﷻ gives them this Awn (عون) from him, this assistance from Him.

Dreams could be a Warning or a Glad Tiding from Allāh ﷻ: Most of the times, if a dream is a glad tiding from Allāh ﷻ, to the believer, it would take a long time for it to occur, while if it is a warning because some dreams could be a warning from Allāh ﷻ, person could deviate from the true path and Allāh ﷻ inspires him with a dream to wake him up. That usually occurs swiftly. For example, the dream of Yūsuf عليه السلام, took a very long time for it to happen, some say something around the figure of 40 years. That's very long time for it to happen. And why? some of the scholars say that the reason why it takes a long time for the dream of glad tiding to occur is because Allāh ﷻ gives the believer, the glad tidings early on, to give him confidence and hope, to inspire him during his life. While if it is a warning, you would see it and it would occur very soon, so that it would not put fear in your heart. So, for example, if a person sees a dream where Allāh ﷻ is warning him, it would happen and it would be over with soon so that the person would not carry that concern in his heart for a very long time. والله أعلم

Dreams are not Source of Legislation: Dreams are glad tidings and warnings, but are not a source of legislation, there are not a source of Shariah. You cannot say that I saw a dream where Allāh ﷻ told me that rather than praying five times a day, I should only pray three, or I should only pray once, or I saw in a dream that such a thing is harām (حرام) or I saw in the dream that such a thing as Halāl (حلال). No, that's not true. Dreams are not a source of the Shariah.

And as mentioned that Abdul Qādir Al Jailānī رحمه الله, he saw a dream, where a voice was talking to him from a cloud and telling him that you have reached a very high status now, and you do not need, you do not need to worship Allāh through the rituals of worship anymore. You have reached a very high level, in spirituality that now you can deal directly with Allāh ﷻ, you don't have to pray and you don't have to fast and you don't have to do Zakah زكاة)) all of these things are things of the past. Abdul Qādir Al Jailānī رحمه الله told him, “Be silent you enemy of Allāh”. So, he knew that this is from shaytān because Allāh ﷻ would not tell his servant that you do not need to worship me anymore.

Ash Shātbi رحمه الله says, araby He says that the benefit of the dream is in giving the believer a glad tiding or a warning, not in legislation, and judgment, or rulings.

True Dreams are Concise and Short: If you saw a dream that's very long, it's like a movie. Or you saw a dream where someone is chasing you and never ends. Most likely that dream doesn't mean anything. True dreams are short and concise. These long, winding dreams, never ending dreams, are meaningless. And sometimes they could be from shaytān (شيطان) like these chasing dreams where you wake up so exhausted and tired. Someone has been chasing him all night long, and you're going up mountains and coming down and going up staircases and coming down and it's never ending. That doesn't mean anything. Say, أعُوْذ بِاللّٰهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطٰانِ الرَّجِيْمwhen you wake up.

The Dream of a Believer Pleases him: The dream of a believer pleases him, but does not make him proud or overconfident. Ibn Muflih رضي الله عنه mentions in his book, Al Adāb ash-Shar‘iyah(آداب الشريعة), he said, araby

He said, Ibrāhīm al-Humaydi was the righteous man and Imām Ahmad bin Hanbal رحمه الله visited him. So, Ibrāhīm al-Humaydi, he told Imām Ahmad bin Hanbal رحمه الله that my mother has seen a dream for you where she saw this and that for you. And then he mentioned in other words, the mother of Ibrāhīm dreamed that the Imām Ahmad bun Hanbal رحمه الله was in Jannah. So, what was the response of Imam Ahmad رحمه الله? out of his humbleness رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, he said, “my brother, Sahl Ibn Salāmah! people used to see dreams for him, similar to what you mentioned, and in the end, he ended up shedding blood.”

So, the dream pleases the believer but it doesn’t make him boastful, it doesn’t make him over confident. And this is very important. If you see a good dream, it is a glad tiding from Allāh ﷻ and be happy with it, but don't be overconfident in its meaning and don't take it as something that is certain because as we mentioned before, the world of dreams is a very complicated and delicate and sophisticated one. So, you can take nothing for granted. If a person dreams that he is in Jannah, don't take that for granted and don't be boastful about it and don't be overconfident about it and think that khalāsa, it's done for me. No, take it as a glad tiding, take it as an indication. Take it for what it's worth.

Dream Interpretation is not Certain but Presumptive: Dream interpretation is not certain but presumptive as Allāh ﷻ says in Qur’ān (قرآن), Yūsuf عليه السلام interpreted the dreams to the prisoners, he said,

And he said to the one who we presumed would be saved.

So, even Yūsuf عليه السلام in his dream interpretation wasn't so certain about it but he presumed that this is the correct interpretation.

And Ibn Kathīr رحمه الله mentions in his book,Al Bidāyah wan Nihāyah, the beginning and the end, that one of the Khulafā(خلفا), Ibn Abbās, And this wasn't a very good Khalīfah(خليفة), he saw a dream where he is climbing a ladder with 28 steps. So, he had that dream interpreted, the ones who interpreted the dream for him, told him that the meaning of this dream is that you would rule for 28 years. Your Khilāfah(خلافة) would be 28 years, each step, represents one year. He died six months later. Subhān Allāh! So, the period of his Khilāfah(خلافة)  was only six months, and he thought that he gonna rule for 28 years according to his dream. Well, there was a mistake here. He died at the age of 28. So, the steps were representative of his age and not his rule. So, see how this dream deceived him.

Another example, there was a woman, she had a daughter and then she dreamed that her daughter would break three banners, The flags, the banner that is carried in wartime. She dreamed that her daughter would break three banners, she went to Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله, and she had that dream interpreted, he told her araby**

he said if her dream is true, it means that she would marry three noble men and all of them would be killed because she's carrying these banners so these banners represent noble men, and when she broke them, it means that they would be killed. Well, she grew up, and she married Yazīd ibn Muhallab, and this was a very great leader in ‘Irāq (عراق), and he was killed. And then she married ‘Amr ibn Yazīd at-Taymi, and he was killed. And then she married, al-Hasan ibn ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Abdur Rahmān ibn ‘Awf رحمه الله, the grandson of the great Sahābi (صحابي), ‘Abdur Rahmān ibn ‘Awf, one of the 10 who are given the glad tidings of Jannah. She had an argument with him, dispute. She told him, you would be killed in the name of Allāh, you would be killed. She was angry so she told him. Probably she didn't tell him the meaning of this dream. Early on she only told him now and she was angry with him, she told him, that you will be killed. So, he told her why is that, so she told him about her dream. He said, Alright, fine, I divorce you. Do you think that I'm going to be killed now? So, she then married the man called al- ‘Abbās ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Hārith ibn Nawfal ibn Hārith ibn ‘Abdul Muttalib from Banu Hāshim (بنو هاشم) , and he was killed. See here, she thought that her husband, Al Hassan would be killed. But the dream was true in the fact that she would marry three men who would be killed but it occurred that her fourth husband was the one who was killed, and not the third.

Another example of how a dream could deceive and its meaning, when it's not interpreted correctly. One man saw during the plague that caskets are coming out from his house, dead bodies are coming out from his house, and the number of these bodies was the same number of his family. So, he interpreted the dream to mean that his entire family would be killed by the plague and Subhān Allāh! the dream started to manifest itself, his family were dying one after the other. And all of these dead bodies were coming out from his house, exactly as he saw in his dream until he was the last member of his family left, so he was pretty sure that he would be killed by the plague. Because his dream, until now, was true. Subhān Allāh! A thief came into his house and was struck by the plague, and he fell ill in his house and Subhān Allāh! he died and he was the last body to leave the house and not the person who saw the dream, he Subhān Allāh! lived. So, you can see here how dreams, Subhān Allāh! sometimes can carry an unexpected, meaning.

The Punishment for Lying about a Dream: The punishment for lying in a dream. It is harām (حرام), and a great sin to claim that you have seen a dream, when you have not seen it or to lie in one's dream to lie in the details of it.

Rusulullāh ﷺ says, “whoever claims to have seen a dream that he has not seen would be told to tie between two hairs on the Day of Judgment, two fine hairs, two fine pieces of hair, a person would be called to tie a knot with these two pieces of hair on the Day of Judgment.”

Such a difficult task would be given to the person who lies in his dreams, on the day of judgment. And Subhān Allāh! there are some who lie in their dreams, to give the people the understanding that their righteous, for example, a person would say and I've seen Rusulullāh ﷺ in my dream, and he told me this and that, a person would do this to show off (الرياء), to give the people a certain image of himself. He is such a righteous person who is seeing a Rusulullāh ﷺ in his dreams. It is harām (حرام) and a grave sin to do so.

A Dream could be seen by a Person, but it is for Someone else: A dream could be seen by a person, but it is for someone else. Al Hākim رحمه الله narrates and Ibn Mubārak رحمه الله, that some people saw a dream for Abū Jahl, that he became a Muslim, and he pledged allegiance to Rusulullāh ﷺ, now Abū Jahl never did that. So, this dream was for his son, ‘Ikramah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه because ‘Ikramah رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, is the one who became a Muslim and pledged allegiance to Rusulullāh ﷺ.

And the dream was seen for Usayd bin Abil ‘Ās رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه, that he became the governor of Mecca(مكة), and he never did. But his son, ‘Attāb, was the one who became the governor of Mecca(مكة). So sometimes a person would see himself, or someone else would see him in a dream. But the dream is for his friend or relative or son, that could happen. It is rare but it could happen. As we have seen in these two examples.

Same Symbol in a Dream could mean Different Things for Different People: The same dream, or the same symbol in a dream could mean different things for different people. For example, a man came to Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله and said that I saw myself making Adhān (أذان) in my dream. Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله told him you will make Hajj, another man came to Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله and said, I saw myself making Adhān (أذان) in my dream. Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله told him, you are a thief. Why did you tell him you are a thief, and he told the other person that you will make Hajj (حج). Ibn Sīrīn رحمه الله was asked this question. He said, Because I saw the first man, I saw in his face righteousness. And Allāh ﷻ says in Qur’ān (قرآن) that Ibrāhīm made Adhān (أذان) calling people to hajj, so I interpreted it to mean that this person will make Hajj While I saw evil in the face of this other man. And Allāh ﷻ says in the Qur’ān (قرآن), in Surah Yūsuf,

So, a person made Adhān (أذان) call because Adhān means call, that you caravan are thieves. So, I interpreted it to mean that this person is a thief.

A Dream is as it is Interpreted: There's a Hadīth(حديث) that Rusulullāh ﷺ said, A dream is hanging on the leg of a bird and another narration on the wing of a bird. As soon as it is interpreted it happens, as it was interpreted. So some scholars say, if you take your dream, to a scholar for interpretation, the dream would occur as it was interpreted and that's why they say you should only mention it to a person who has knowledge about dream interpretation, and as Rusulullāh ﷺ said, أؤ ناصح , or person who would give you sincere advice and he should not tell your dream to a person who is envious or hates you or would not give you sincere advice, because he could interpret that dream wrong, and it would occur as it was interpreted.

However, there is a difference of opinion regarding this issue and Ibn Hajar رحمه الله says that the dream is not according to the first interpretation that is given to it, and he says this, regarding a dream that was seen by someone, and this dream was presented to Rusulullāh ﷺ, Abu Bakar رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنه said, Yaa Rusulullāh ﷺ! let me interpret the dream. We'll talk about that in detail when it comes up. But anyway, Ibn Hajar رحمه الله says that there is a difference of opinion regarding this issue so Some scholars say that it occurs according to its interpretation and some scholars say that it doesn't. Anyway, as we mentioned, this is a very complicated and delicate world.

These are 17 rules and notes regarding dream interpretation. In next lectures, In Shaa Allāh will talk about dreams that were mentioned in Qur’ān (قرآن) and mentioned in Hadīth (حديث).
